name: Agent — ask, approve, resume (closes the HITL loop)

nodes.name: Ask the agent
nodes.notes:
http://agent:8000 — the compose network, not the public URL. Nothing leaves the host.
Header Auth credential: name = Authorization, value = 'Bearer <AGENT_API_KEY>'.
thread_id is what /resume later addresses, so it must be stable for this execution.
Timeout 300s: the verifier can loop up to 3 attempts.

nodes.name: Approval needed?
nodes.notes: The agent pauses at interrupt() BEFORE any side effect. If it answered without proposing an action, status is 'complete' and there is nothing to approve.

parameters.subject: =Approve: {{ $json.approval.action }}

nodes.name: Human approval
nodes.notes:
Gmail send-and-wait. The node emails the reviewer with Approve / Disapprove buttons and PAUSES this workflow until one is clicked.

Output is {data:{approved:boolean}} — verified against the node's own schema, not assumed.

The reviewer sees the ANSWER and the EVIDENCE, not just an action name. Approving 'create_compliance_ticket' with no visible justification is rubber-stamping with extra steps.

Swap this node for Slack or a Wait/form node if you prefer — nothing else in the workflow changes.

nodes.name: Resume the agent
nodes.notes:
THIS IS THE STEP THAT CLOSES THE LOOP.

The agent has been paused since 'Ask the agent' returned. Its state is persisted in a checkpoint, so the pause survives an agent container restart — verified by killing the container mid-pause and resuming afterwards.

The graph continues from the checkpoint and only NOW fires the agent-action webhook, which workflow 2 receives.

A rejection is also recorded rather than dropped: 'a human declined this' is an audit fact.

assignments.name: note
assignments.value: Agent answered without proposing an action — nothing to approve.
